title: Super Micro stock sinks 5% despite $19.9 billion quarter
detail:
Super Micro stock sinks 5% despite $19.9 billion quarter
Faizan Farooque
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 11:07 AM MST 1 min read
SMCI
CRWV
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Super Micro Computer Inc. (SMCI, Financials) shares dipped around 5% , erasing some of the gains from the previous session, as investors continued to weigh the company's cash-flow and working-capital demands.Shares were down $1.61 to about $28.80 from closing. Shares gained almost 10% on Wednesday in a wider tech surge led by good earnings from AI-cloud provider CoreWeave.Even with the bounce, Super Micro is still down more than 28% in the previous month.The corporation recently reported over $19.9 billion in revenue for its fiscal first quarter and gave second-quarter projections above forecasts.The company also said its cash conversion cycle improved to 97 days from 149 days. But free cash flow remained negative at $481 million, raising doubts about the cost of funding strong sales growth.Analysts have also flagged increasing borrowing costs, concentration of customers and inventory levels as possible problems.Super Micro's AI server business continues to grow. The business said Wednesday that it has begun shipping its H15 server systems with AMD's sixth-generation EPYC 9006 CPUs.The systems address workloads for cloud, high-performance computing and AI. Super Micro trades at around 4.67 times projected non-GAAP profits, but its cheap value is a function of cash generation difficulties and financial risk.Investors will be looking to next quarterly earnings for evidence that greater sales will convert to positive free cash flow.

title: Supermicro, Nvidia Reportedly Face DOJ Scrutiny In Separate Inquiries — SMCI Stock Plunges
detail:
Supermicro, Nvidia Reportedly Face DOJ Scrutiny In Separate Inquiries — SMCI Stock Plunges
Harshita Tyagi
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 10:58 AM MST 4 min read
SMCI
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Two DOJ inquiries involving Supermicro and Megaspeed focus on Alice Huang, Semafor reported.

A separate DOJ antitrust investigation focuses specifically on Nvidia, but Jensen Huang is not a target of U.S. law enforcement investigations, Bloomberg said.

The report about the investigations comes amid Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO on Thursday following reports of two extramarital affairs.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI) shares fell more than 12% on Thursday after a reported U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) inquiry into the AI server maker focused on Alice Huang, a woman U.S. officials suspect has ties to Chinese intelligence.

A Semafor report, citing two administration officials, said multiple DOJ probes could involve Nvidia (NVDA). One investigation focuses specifically on Nvidia over antitrust concerns, while two other inquiries involve Supermicro and Megaspeed International.

The publication said there was no indication the DOJ would seek criminal charges against Nvidia or Jensen Huang at this time.

The report about the investigations comes amid Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO on Thursday following reports of two extramarital affairs, including one involving Alice Huang, whom U.S. authorities reportedly suspect of ties to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO and began searching for a permanent successor.

Scrutiny Of Possible Chip Smuggling

Separately, Bloomberg also reported that the DOJ is investigating whether entities linked to Alice Huang were involved in efforts to smuggle Supermicro products into China.

The inquiry is being led by the U.S. Attorney's Office in Manhattan, the report said, citing a person familiar with the matter. It remains unclear whether the investigation is connected to existing chip-smuggling cases in the U.S. or Asia, or what role Huang or entities linked to her may have played.

The DOJ is investigating Huang's former company, Megaspeed, over suspected semiconductor smuggling. The company has denied wrongdoing. The publication said prosecutors are separately conducting an espionage investigation examining Alice Huang's relationship with Jensen Huang.

The former Nvidia CEO is not a target of U.S. law enforcement investigations, per the Bloomberg report.

Stocktwits reached out to Nvidia and Supermicro for comment but has not received a response til the time of this publication.

The previously unreported scrutiny is being led by the US attorney's office in Manhattan, according to a person familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg. It remains unclear whether the investigation is connected to existing semiconductor-smuggling cases brought by US or Asian prosecutors.

The development comes as the DOJ is already investigating Alice Huang's former company, Megaspeed International, over suspected semiconductor smuggling. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing.

The allegations also intersect with an existing criminal case involving Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw, whom Manhattan federal prosecutors charged in March alongside two others over an alleged conspiracy to ship Nvidia-powered servers to an unnamed Southeast Asian company before diverting them to Chinese customers.

Super Micro was not named as a defendant and has said it is cooperating with the investigation. Liaw, who pleaded not guilty, is no longer with the company.

One is specifically focused on the chipmaker on antitrust grounds, while separate inquiries concern Megaspeed and Super Micro and have focused on Alice Huang's involvement.

The reports come amid the fallout from Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia. Nvidia shares remained down around 5% following the announcement, as investors assessed the implications for the company and its leadership.

There is currently no indication that prosecutors intend to bring criminal charges against Nvidia or Jensen Huang. It is also unclear what role, if any, Alice Huang or entities connected to her may have played in the alleged smuggling of Super Micro products. DOJ investigations can conclude without charges.

title: How Risky Is Hewlett Packard Enterprise Stock?
detail:
How Risky Is Hewlett Packard Enterprise Stock?
Trefis Team
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 10:10 AM MST 3 min read
HPE
DELL
^GSPC
IBM
CSCO
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) lost 27.0% in the month to November 11, 2026, while the S&P 500 slipped 2.3%. The decline occurred between earnings reports. Over the same dates, Dell Technologies fell 34.6%. Although the shares are still up 114.2% over twelve months, the drop since October 13 shows how quickly the stock can give ground. So how far has Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock fallen when the whole market sold off?

HPE Stock Has Fallen Further Than The Market

During market shocks, HPE stock has usually dropped more than the S&P 500 before returning to its earlier high within months. The company has traded through 10 shocks since listing in November 2015, two of which share one 2015-16 fall. Across its 9 separate falls, the stock fell 23.6% on average, against 15.1% for the S&P 500.

The deepest decline in a market shock occurred during the 2020 COVID-19 crash, when HPE lost 45.3% and the index lost 33.7%. The 2025 US tariff shock came close, with the stock falling 42.3% against 18.8% for the S&P 500. The 2022 inflation shock was the only time HPE fell no further than the market: 23.9%, against 24.5% for the S&P 500.

The stock has also recovered every time. After each of the 9 falls, shares returned to their highest close before the low, taking a median of 4.2 months from the bottom. The slowest return followed the COVID-19 crash and took 10.6 months.

How Has Hewlett Packard Enterprise's Business Changed Since 2024?

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is a much bigger company than a year ago. It sold $41.9 billion over the twelve months to July 31, 2026, up 26.6% from a year earlier, and that is faster than the 14.0% growth of the twelve months before. These are reported figures; management's call figures are adjusted to include Juniper Networks, which HPE is integrating, from the start of fiscal 2025.

Profit has grown alongside sales. In fiscal Q3 2026, the GAAP operating margin reached 11.4%, compared with 2.7% in the same quarter of 2025.

HPE carries more debt than it did two years ago. Total debt stood at $20.2 billion on July 31, 2026, compared to $11.8 billion in July 2024, though the balance has declined from $23.7 billion a year earlier. That debt equals 30.2% of the company's market value, against 19.5% for the S&P 500.

Where Is Hewlett Packard Enterprise Under Pressure Now?

HPE has lacked the components necessary to meet demand. On the company's September 2, 2026 call, management said supply constraints continue to limit the volume of orders it can ship, and that memory chips such as DDR5 and NAND have been short since the beginning of 2026. Management said data center networking revenue declined 6% in fiscal Q3 on a normalized basis, which counts Juniper in both years, because of shipment timing driven by supply constraints.
